title: Florida House, District 41
what_it_does: Represents District 41 in the Florida House of Representatives; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: Incumbent Democratic Rep. Bruce Antone sought re-election. ClickOrlando (Feb. 2026) reported Antone would face Jane't Buford-Johnson in the Aug. 18 Democratic primary and that a Republican identified as Lincoln-McCreight was unopposed for the Republican nomination, with the general election Nov. 3. Neither the final qualified field nor the primary result could be verified; the News Service of Florida's post-primary list of Democratic incumbents who faced challengers did not include Antone, which may mean the primary challenge did not materialize.
verified_ballot_note: ClickOrlando, Feb. 24, 2026: 'Antone will face Jane't Buford-Johnson in the Aug. 18 Democratic primary. At the moment, Lincoln-McCreight is unopposed in the Aug. 18 Republican primary. The general election will be held Nov. 3' (https://www.clickorlando.com/election-2026/2026/02/24/florida-house-candidate-from-viral-n-word-video-seeks-to-unseat-rep-bruce-antone/). Post-qualifying and post-primary status unverified. Research limitation: every WebFetch (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, Division of Elections, county SOEs, news sites) was blocked and the search budget was capped, so this roster comes only from search-result snippets and should be re-verified against the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.photo_source: Florida House member page (MemberId=4269); image URL not verified
candidates.background: Incumbent Democratic state representative for HD 41 (Orange County), age 65 per ClickOrlando; has served the district since 2022 and previously served in the House. Filed for re-election in 2026.

taxes.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

property_tax.summary: Voted against CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; a vote to refer the amendment is coded as leaning.

housing.summary: Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.

immigration.summary: Voted against SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.

Voted against SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.
Voted against HB 543 (2023), the 2023 law allowing adults to carry a concealed firearm without a permit.
Voted against HB 1 (2023), the 2023 law that made every Florida student eligible for a state-funded scholarship usable at private schools or for home education.
Voted against SB 254 (2023), the 2023 law barring gender-affirming medical treatment for minors and restricting it for adults.
Voted against SB 7050 (2023), the 2023 elections law that raised penalties and shortened deadlines for third-party voter-registration groups and changed vote-by-mail and voter-roll procedures.
